newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen tracking sideways.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen tracking sideways.

text.p: Belgian shares were seen tracking sideways in the coming days after coming off early highs on Wednesday to mostly post only modest gains.

Despite a firm dollar and stronger bonds, the Bel-20 leading share index .BFX ended up just 6.41 points, or 0.30 percent, at 2,120.84 points with 13 winners and seven losers. The index had risen as high as 2,129.40 mid session.
"There's very little activity by fundamental investors. We are still in holiday mode," one trader said. "Volumes are pretty modest and I expect will stay like that until next week."

Delhaize was again the most active Bel-20 stock, but volumes were more modest than seen at the start of the week in a sell-off sparked by disappointment at its U.S. Food Lion unit. Delhaize bounced back 20 francs to 1,780 francs, with both KB Securities and Bank Degroof maintaining their positive ratings on the share despite Food Lion's woes.

Holding company Societe Generale de Belgique was also moderately active, rising 15 francs to 3,000 francs ahead of the board meeting on Friday of its French parent Suez to discuss a merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
Oil group PetroFina rose 100 francs to 12,025 francs as news of expansion of its U.S. petrochemical business was well received.

But chemicals group Solvay fell back 225 francs to 20,250 francs. Dealers said news it was increasing its stake in a U.S. plastics unit, although good in itself, was not enough to brake profit taking on the stocks recent rise that has been sparked by worries about its core alkalis business.
Photo processing group Spector rose 4.55 percent to 2,300 francs as a company roadshow among Brussels brokerages on 1996 results drew new buyers for the stock.
Holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren also rose 3.69 percent to 6,750 francs, with investors eyeing possible earnings growth from a buoyant dredging sector.
